page: Vultr vcg-a40-12c-60g-24vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor. The system provides 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It features 60.0 GB of system memory, yielding 5.0 GB per core. Acceleration is provided by a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU, delivering 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 1110 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks place this server in the average tier across multiple categories. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1631.08, while the multi-core score reaches 20624.31. Memory bandwidth testing shows a read-only small block cached speed of 1186.32 GB/sec, which drops to 123.01 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, and a write speed of 53.08 GB/sec. In database and application testing, the instance achieves 22.59 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads and a static web serving throughput of 20.12 GB/sec.

For machine learning workloads, the fractional A40 GPU handles smaller models efficiently, processing prompts at 1048.4 tokens per second and text generation at 219.1 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model. However, performance drops significantly on larger models; prompt processing for a 7B parameter model is weak at 23.45 tokens per second, indicating a clear tradeoff when scaling to medium-sized LLMs. This resource profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for developers requiring dedicated GPU memory and local NVMe storage without the expense of a full GPU. It is suited for small-scale LLM inference, database operations, and general-purpose GPU-accelerated workloads.
